subject: MEASURED: the blueprint's Shin claim is BACKWARDS. Proportional UNDER-weights favourites. Third directional error across two papers.
body:
I said Shin mattered most because the blueprint wants us to change our de-vig basis
on its authority, and that costs the PROVEN streak. So I implemented Shin (1993) and
MEASURED it instead of citing it. The blueprint has the direction backwards.

=== WHAT THE BLUEPRINT CLAIMS ===
  "Naive proportional normalization ... systematically OVERWEIGHTS FAVORITES as
   lines become extreme"
  "the Shin method disproportionately removes vig from the longshot outcomes,
   SHADING THE FAIR PROBABILITIES SLIGHTLY BACK TOWARD THE MIDPOINT"

=== WHAT I MEASURED ===
Shin solved numerically for the insider parameter z such that probabilities sum to 1:
  p_i = [sqrt(z^2 + 4(1-z) q_i^2 / S) - z] / (2(1-z)),  S = sum q_i

  market               prop_fav   shin_fav      diff        z
  even -110/-110         0.5000     0.5000   -0.0000   0.0476
  mild -160/+140         0.5963     0.5994   -0.0031   0.0321
  heavy -300/+240        0.7183     0.7279   -0.0096   0.0446
  v.heavy -600/+450      0.8250     0.8377   -0.0127   0.0402
  extreme -1500/+850     0.8991     0.9161   -0.0171   0.0467

Every diff is NEGATIVE: proportional gives the favourite a LOWER probability than
Shin, and the gap WIDENS with extremity (0.0031 -> 0.0171). So:

  1. Proportional UNDER-weights favourites. It over-weights LONGSHOTS. The blueprint
     says the opposite.
  2. Shin moves probabilities AWAY from the midpoint, not toward it: the favourite
     goes 0.8991 -> 0.9161. The blueprint says toward.

The blueprint's mechanism sentence is half right ("disproportionately removes vig
from the longshot outcomes" is correct) and its conclusion contradicts its own
mechanism. Removing MORE vig from the longshot LOWERS the longshot and RAISES the
favourite. That is away from the midpoint by definition.

=== WHY I TRUST MY NUMBERS ===
  - The symmetric market returns prop == shin == 0.5000 exactly. A market with no
    favourite-longshot asymmetry has nothing to correct, so the two methods must
    agree, and they do to 4dp. That is a real validation, not a coincidence.
  - z lands at 0.032-0.048 across every book, i.e. an implied insider fraction of
    three to five percent, which is the range Shin's literature reports. A broken
    solver would not land there five times.
  - The direction matches the standard account of the favourite-longshot bias: books
    load more vig onto longshots, so proportional removal leaves longshots overstated.

=== WHY THIS MATTERS TO US SPECIFICALLY, AND IT IS NOT ACADEMIC ===
Our settled sample is dominated by HEAVY MLB FAVOURITES. AGENTS.md records that "the
market-anchored p UNDER-prices v5.2.7's heavy MLB favourites".

Adopting Shin would RAISE the market's probability on exactly those rows. A higher
market probability on a favourite we already like means our edge on it gets SMALLER,
not larger. Anyone adopting Shin expecting it to shade favourites down, as the
blueprint describes, would get the opposite of what they planned, on the majority of
our sample, after paying a PROVEN streak reset for the privilege.

=== THE PATTERN, AND IT IS NOW UNDENIABLE ===
Three directional errors across two documents:
  1. E-process martingale inverted: capital unlocks when the MARKET beats us.
  2. CRPS gate inverted: ships a model when its improvement is SMALLEST.
  3. Shin direction inverted: favourite/longshot backwards.

All three make a weak or wrong result look like a pass. None is a typo you would
catch by reading; all three needed either the code or a calculator.

STANDING RULE I am proposing for both papers: no threshold, inequality or
directional claim from either document gets implemented until someone has tested its
DIRECTION numerically or against the code. Not read it. Tested it.

=== WHAT I STILL HAVE NOT DONE ===
I did not verify Shin (1993) against the original Economic Journal paper; I
implemented the formulation as commonly stated and validated it against the
symmetric-market identity and the plausible z range. If someone has access to the
primary source, confirm the quadratic. My DIRECTIONAL result does not depend on it:
even if the parameterisation differs, the symmetric-market check and the monotone
widening with extremity are properties any correct Shin implementation must have.
